about: Data of case file CF3 (where should hydrogen go when nobody knows how much wind will be built?). Every sentence about the study is approved excerpt wording (reports/learn/excerpts_for_approval.md, E10 and E11, approved 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-05), word for word. The toy ('idea') is lesson M8's: its data and plans are read from m08-stochastic-robust.json.

events.label: Journal article (this case)
events.text: Electrolyzers, hydrogen tanks and fuel cells are sized for [[ercot|ERCOT]]'s eight weather zones under uncertain renewable build-out and electricity demand, with hydrogen pipelines between neighbouring zones; published online on 2 March 2025, in the March 2025 issue.

source.label: Li et al. (2025), International Journal of Hydrogen Energy 113, 77–89

events.label: Code released
events.text: A documented, runnable implementation of the planning framework, with synthetic examples (version 1.0.2).

boundary.title: Where the result holds
holds: [[ercot|ERCOT]]'s eight weather zones, every hour of one year, in nine scenarios of renewable build-out and electricity demand;
hydrogen demand is held fixed across scenarios;
the CO₂ from gas plants and reformers is captured and stored at a cost;
the emissions result comes from sensitivity runs in which power from gas-fired plants became more expensive.
leaves: truck and rail transport of hydrogen.
boundary.source: From the approved excerpt of Li et al. (2025), International Journal of Hydrogen Energy.

idea.title: Size it before the wind is built
idea.note: M8's toy: one windy zone, three build-outs with chances 25%, 50% and 25%, illustrative round numbers in 2025 dollars.
